title: Subarrays With at Least K Distinct
statement:
Given an array `nums` of `n` integers and an integer `k`, count the **contiguous subarrays** that contain **at least `k` distinct values**.

Repeated values inside a subarray count only once towards its number of distinct values. Subarrays are counted by their position, so two subarrays with the same contents at different positions are counted separately.

Print the number of such subarrays. The answer can exceed the range of a 32-bit integer.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers, the elements of `nums`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer, the number of subarrays with at least `k` distinct values.

examples.explanation: There are 10 subarrays. The four single-element subarrays have one distinct value, and no other subarray is constant, so the other 6 have at least 2 distinct values.
Every subarray has exactly one distinct value, which is fewer than 2.
Only subarrays of length 3 or more can have 3 distinct values: [1,2,3], [2,3,4] and [1,2,3,4].

hints: Counting subarrays with at least k distinct values directly is awkward. Count the complement: all subarrays minus those with at most k - 1 distinct values.
Subarrays with at most m distinct values can be counted with a sliding window: for each right end, the valid left ends form a contiguous range.
Keep a frequency map and shrink the left side while the window has more than m distinct values; add right - left + 1 for each right end.
